title: Change two values in a config file open in Mousepad, and save it

capabilities.why: Mousepad, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

setup.why: Write the config file in the run's folder.

argv: d=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; rm -rf $d && mkdir -p $d && printf '%s\n' '# app-{{nonce}}' 'name = app-{{nonce}}' 'port = {{conf.port}}' 'log_level = {{conf.level}}' 'workers = 4' > $d/app-{{nonce}}.conf

setup.why: Open the config file in Mousepad.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec mousepad /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/app-{{nonce}}.conf

setup.why: Wait for Mousepad's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, put the pointer on it and activate it: a window manager gives the keys to the window activated, and with none they go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class mousepad | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Mousepad window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); xdotool windowactivate $w 2>/dev/null; sleep 1

instruction: Mousepad has app-{{nonce}}.conf open. Change the port to {{conf.newport}} and the log_level to {{conf.newlevel}}, keep every other line as it is, and save the file.

checks.why: The saved file holds the five lines with the new port and log level and the other three unchanged (leading and trailing blank space aside). Setup wrote the old values, so an agent that does nothing fails, and so does one that saves only one of the two.

teardown.why: Close Mousepad without saving (KILL: Mousepad holds on to a changed document on TERM) and delete the run's folder.

oracle.why: Select all (Ctrl+A) and type the file back with the two new values, then Save (Ctrl+S): the file has a name, so no dialog.
